scope: binding_strength_4way metric definition + falsifier preregistration (per #92 honest C3 #3, F1 v2 §3)

BSE-1_pearson_cross_corr_mean.rationale: matches N-1 BRIDGE 4-gate convention; immediately computable on existing W4 + N-1 data; reproducible

BSE-2_granger_causality_directed_sum.rationale: captures asymmetric coupling (e.g. tension → CLM 단방향) but requires stationarity (W4 frozen-fixed-point violates)

BSE-3_transfer_entropy_kraskov.formula: binding_strength = (1/n_directed_pairs) · Σ TE(X_i → X_j) [KSG estimator k=4]
BSE-3_transfer_entropy_kraskov.rationale: model-free, IIT-aligned (information transfer); BUT W1 estimator artifact precedent → use only as falsifier sanity check on BSE-1 PASS

F-ARTIFACT.verdict_contribution: DOWNGRADED — measurement invalidated, retry with new estimator

random_shuffle_control_protocol.method: Per substrate i, shuffle time-axis indices independently with fresh seed (numpy default_rng(seed=42 + i)). Recompute binding_strength on shuffled data. Repeat 100 trials. F-ARTIFACT triggers if observed binding within ±0.02 of random-shuffle mean.

honest_c3: BSE-1 Pearson assumes linear coupling — nonlinear 4-way binding (e.g. multiplicative cross-substrate gating) would underestimate. BSE-3 TE secondary check captures nonlinear but with estimator artifact tail risk (W1 precedent).

z-score normalization per substrate masks substrate-specific signal magnitude — high-magnitude tension events get same weight as low-magnitude EEG fluctuations. Alternative (raw correlation) introduces scale bias. Trade-off acknowledged.

random_shuffle control breaks time-correlation structure but preserves marginal distribution — false positive ~5% expected at ±0.02 band even on truly independent data. F-ARTIFACT threshold may need calibration after first P1 measurement.

X_tension data source 'tension_bridge.hexa UDP 9999 capture' is anima-internal benchmark only — peer-review external validation 0. binding_strength involving X_tension is anima-specific, not transferable to other consciousness frameworks.
